raw_response:
I've been farming this land in Quzhou for more than 30 years, and I know what works here. My family has about 8 mu total. I will plant 5 mu with winter wheat and follow it immediately with summer maize on the same plots — that's our double-crop rotation, and it gives us both grain to eat and some to sell. The other 3 mu I will put in cotton because the price has been steady and my neighbor Lao Wang's cotton did well last year. 

For the wheat, I will rotary till the soil before sowing in early October, use an improved seed variety I've bought from the village supply shop, put down about 15 kg of nitrogen per mu along with some compound fertilizer for phosphorus and potassium, irrigate three times, and spray four times for weeds and bugs. I expect around 450 kg per mu if the spring rain comes. For the summer maize, there is no time to plough after wheat harvest — everyone here plants no-till into the wheat stubble in mid-June. I will use hybrid seed, about 13 kg nitrogen per mu, irrigate twice, spray three times, and hope for 500 kg per mu. For cotton, I will rotary till in April, plant improved seed, use about 10 kg nitrogen per mu, irrigate twice, and spray fourteen times because cotton bollworm is terrible if you skip even one spray. I keep my fertilizer a bit lower than some neighbors because my husband is working less now and we must watch every yuan, but I won't cut too much — a bad harvest hurts more than saving a few kilograms of urea.
